description: Carrot root fly is a serious insect pest of carrots and related crops. The adult fly lays eggs in the soil near carrot plants. The larvae (maggots) hatch and tunnel into the roots, feeding on the tissues and causing serious damage to the crop.
symptoms: Carrot leaves wilt and become weak
Leaves turn rusty red or yellow
Rusty-brown tunnels under the carrot skin
Reduced yield and poor quality roots
visual_signature: rusty brown tunnels in carrot root
pest_description: Adult flies are small and low-flying
life_cycle: Adult flies lay eggs in soil near carrot plants
Larvae burrow into carrot roots and feed
Larvae develop in soil and later become adult flies
spread: adult flies laying eggs in soil
management: Use crop rotation to avoid planting carrots repeatedly in the same field
Remove infected plants and damaged roots
Use physical barriers such as mesh or insect netting
Use horticultural fleece to cover crops
Plant resistant carrot varieties when available
biological_control: Beneficial nematodes (Steinernema species) applied to soil
Encouraging natural predators of fly larvae
chemical_control: targeted insecticide treatments against larvae (local regulations apply)
prevention: Use fine insect netting around crops
Avoid leaving damaged carrots in the soil
